summary: This program stores the seven letters of the musical scale in a single string and prints each one on its own line. It shows that a for loop can walk through the characters of a string, not just a range of numbers.

lines.text: The whole musical scale lives in one string, seven characters long. Python treats a string as a sequence of characters, which is exactly what makes it loopable.

Here the loop is given a string instead of a range, so `letter` holds one character at a time: first "A", then "B", and so on through "G". Nothing tells the loop to stop after seven turns — it runs out when the string runs out.
Because print adds a newline each time it is called, and it is called once per turn of the loop, the seven notes come out one per line.
